---
title: "Panel and foundation-model forecasting"
---

The `forecast-panel` workflow compares models across related series:
MLForecast with LightGBM or scikit-learn histogram gradient boosting,
NeuralForecast with NHITS, and zero-shot foundation models (FMs) through
[Darts](https://unit8co.github.io/darts/). A dependency-light seasonal baseline
is always available. These capabilities are currently unreleased; from this
checkout use:

```bash
uv sync --extra ml --extra neural --extra foundation --extra viz
uv run ts-agents workflow show forecast-panel --json
```

The base and recommended profiles remain unchanged. The `all` profile includes
every optional backend. All imports of the optional libraries are lazy.
`workflow show forecast-panel` reports status `available` on every install,
because `seasonal_naive` always works; each optional family (`ml_backends`,
`neural_backends`, `foundation_models`, `plots`) appears under
`availability.optional_features` with its missing dependencies and extra.
Requesting an unavailable method fails before any forecasting artifacts are
written (only a failed `run_manifest.json` is recorded), with an install hint
such as ``Install `ts-agents[foundation]`.`` (exit code 3).

To try the workflow on bundled data, export the M4 Monthly mini-panel. The
source stores integer time indexes, so the exported month-start dates are a
synthetic alignment: every train split ends at `--train-end` (default
`2015-06-01`) and the holdout covers the next 18 months.

```bash
uv run ts-agents data export-panel m4-monthly-mini --split train --out panel.csv --json
uv run ts-agents workflow run forecast-panel --input panel.csv --freq MS \
  --horizon 18 --season-length 12 --methods seasonal_naive --skip-plots --json
```

Keep the holdout (`--split holdout`) outside the workflow input and use it only
to score the saved `forecast.csv`.

## Input and execution

Single-series foundation-model adapters require a one-dimensional history and
reject context values outside the finite Float32 range before loading weights.
In `forecast-series`, each foundation model's `model_spec.json` identifies its
actual `forecast_phase` and horizon. Nonwinning models record validation only;
a winning model records its future configuration plus `validation_spec`.

Supply a CSV/TSV/parquet/JSON/JSONL file, tabular JSON, or stdin. The input has
exactly three columns, `unique_id`, `ds`, and `y`; rename them with `--id-col`,
`--time-col`, and `--value-col`. A single series is a panel with one constant ID.
Each series must be regular at the explicit frequency and share an end date;
earlier start dates may differ. Gaps, missing values, duplicate keys, nonfinite
targets, timezone-aware timestamps and extra covariates are rejected. Normalize
timestamps to a documented timezone convention before passing the data.

```bash
uv run ts-agents workflow run forecast-panel \
  --input panel.csv --freq h --horizon 24 \
  --season-length 168 --lags 1,24,168 \
  --methods seasonal_naive,lightgbm,nhits \
  --n-windows 3 --n-estimators 200 --max-steps 1000 \
  --accelerator cpu --output-dir outputs/electricity-validation --json
```

Use `--methods lightgbm,histgbm` for the ML profile or `--methods nhits` for
neural-only runs. LightGBM and histogram GBM receive lag, shifted rolling-mean
and known calendar features. NHITS trains across the whole panel with a
training-only internal validation tail for early stopping. `--input-size`
controls its context. `--accelerator gpu` requests one GPU explicitly; current
local qualification covers CPU only. Native models retain their backend's
dependency requirements when reloaded.

Every backtest origin fits a fresh model on the preceding history; no model is
fit on later panel targets. Origins are spaced by `--step-size` (default:
horizon). There is also a final fit for future forecasts. `--n-estimators` and
`--max-steps` cap each fit, not total runtime. Choose origin counts with this
cost in mind. Resume reruns the compatible computation; it does not load a
training checkpoint. The existing jobs surface provides background execution,
logs, and supervised local cancellation.

## Evaluation and artifacts

Validation MAE/RMSE and training-only seasonal MASE are recorded overall, per
series and per horizon. The ranking uses pooled validation RMSE, which can favor
large-scale series. Zero seasonal scales have undefined MASE and are counted
explicitly. Overlapping origins count different forecasts of the same target.
Use these scores for selection and keep a final test outside the input. Future
forecasts in `forecast.csv` are not scored against invented targets.
`metrics.json` also records `options.context_length` and, when FMs are
requested, `options.resolved_context_length` (per model) and
`foundation_models` (one model spec per FM).

| Artifact | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `metrics.json` | Metrics, settings, quality flags, package versions, per-fit runtime |
| `backtest_predictions.csv` | Series, origin, horizon step, actual, prediction, training MASE scale |
| `forecast.csv` | Future forecasts from every requested model |
| `models/<method>/` | Native persisted model files; baseline stores history; FMs store only `model_spec.json` |
| `backtest.png` | Last validation origin for up to four series |
| `report.md` | Comparison summary, validation boundaries and limitations |
| `run_manifest.json` | Run identity, input fingerprint, options and artifact paths |

The report-generation skill can assemble a comprehensive report from these
artifacts without retraining. To reuse models in Python, use
`MLForecast.load(".../models/lightgbm")` or
`NeuralForecast.load(".../models/nhits")`, then the backend's `predict` method.
Load only model files you trust: native model formats can deserialize Python
objects. This workflow currently offers point forecasts, not calibrated intervals.

## Foundation models (Darts, zero-shot)

Install `ts-agents[foundation]` (`darts[torch]` plus `torch`). Darts is used as
the interoperability layer; `ts-agents` pins a small catalog of checkpoints
rather than acting as a model hub. The same method names work in
`forecast-panel`, `forecast-series`, the `forecast_foundation*` agent tools and
the `foundation-smoke` autoresearch loop.

| Method | Darts class | Checkpoint @ pinned revision | Licence | Weights |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `chronos2_small` (default) | `Chronos2Model` | `autogluon/chronos-2-small` @ `ddec013` | Apache-2.0 | ~112 MB |
| `chronos2` | `Chronos2Model` | `amazon/chronos-2` @ `29ec376` | Apache-2.0 | ~478 MB |
| `timesfm2p5` | `TimesFM2p5Model` | `google/timesfm-2.5-200m-pytorch` @ `1d95242` | Apache-2.0 | ~925 MB |
| `patchtst_fm` | `PatchTSTFMModel` | `ibm-granite/granite-timeseries-patchtst-fm-r1` @ `151f9c6` | Apache-2.0 | ~1032 MB |

Full revisions are in `workflow show forecast-panel --json`
(`capabilities.foundation_model_checkpoints`) and in every run's
`metrics.json`.

```bash
uv run ts-agents workflow run forecast-panel --input panel.csv --freq MS \
  --horizon 18 --season-length 12 --n-windows 2 \
  --methods seasonal_naive,chronos2_small --skip-plots --json
```

- **Zero-shot:** nothing is trained. At every validation origin each FM
  conditions only on that origin's history, so no later target leaks into a
  forecast. The final forecast conditions on the most recent history.
- **Context:** `--context-length` sets how many trailing points each series
  contributes (default 512). It is capped so context plus horizon fits the
  model (8192 points, or 16384 for TimesFM 2.5); an explicit value that does
  not fit fails validation (exit code 2). Horizons above 1024 are rejected.
  Shorter series use all available history. `--input-size` stays NHITS-only.
- **Model notes:** TimesFM 2.5 switches to its longer projection head above
  128 steps. PatchTST-FM was trained for a 64-step horizon and is used
  autoregressively beyond that, which can weaken accuracy.
- **Downloads:** only the requested checkpoints are fetched, into `HF_HOME`, on
  first use. Network-less sandboxes need a pre-populated cache and
  `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`. A checkpoint that is neither cached nor downloadable
  fails with `FoundationModelUnavailableError` ("weights for ... are not
  cached and could not be downloaded"), not with a missing-package error. The
  JSON envelope reports it as `backend_unavailable` (exit code 5,
  `retryable: true`) with the remediation in `hint`. See
  [`SANDBOX.md`](https://github.com/fnauman/ts-agents/blob/main/SANDBOX.md) for
  sandbox-specific notes.
- **Artifacts:** `models/<fm>/` holds only `model_spec.json` (Darts class,
  checkpoint, revision, Darts version, resolved context, accelerator,
  `weights_saved: false`). Weights are never copied into run directories.
- **Resources:** each requested FM stays loaded for the whole run and is
  released at the end; running all four together needs several GB of RAM.
  The `forecast_foundation*` agent tools release weights after every call,
  and direct library calls outside a run keep at most one model loaded.
  `--accelerator gpu` is used only when requested.
- **Interpretation:** public benchmarks such as M4 may overlap FM pretraining
  data, so FM scores on them can be optimistic. FMs produce point forecasts
  only, and they never add quality flags; caveats appear in `report.md`.

[MLForecast documentation](https://nixtlaverse.nixtla.io/mlforecast/forecast.html),
[NHITS documentation](https://nixtlaverse.nixtla.io/neuralforecast/models.nhits.html)
and the [Darts foundation-model documentation](https://unit8co.github.io/darts/)
describe the underlying interfaces.
[MLForecast documentation](https://nixtlaverse.nixtla.io/mlforecast/forecast.html)
and [NHITS documentation](https://nixtlaverse.nixtla.io/neuralforecast/models.nhits.html)
describe the underlying training interfaces.

Requested input columns must exist; missing custom names fail even when the default
columns exist. Default lag offsets are deduplicated for a season length of one.
Explicit empty method lists are rejected. Sandbox exports preserve model subdirectories.
